reason: Conversation 1 refuses to engage at all with an in-scope, benign question, leaving a worried homeowner with no reassurance beyond a generic safety line and a pointless pointer to an engineer. Conversation 2 correctly identifies the hidden truth up front (condenser in the side walls, warmth is normal, not a fire risk), confirms the no-smell/no-scorching boundary, and ends with the right 'can keep your hand on it and it cools fine, so it's normal' reassurance. Its weaknesses are real but secondary: it overstates the 1cm gap as 'too tight' and 'explains why', pads with irrelevant suggestions (heat mat under feet, 24-hour settling, blocked vents), ignores the refusal to move the unit, repeats itself verbatim, and never advises checking the manual's exact clearances or the plug temperature, but it still lands the honest, correct diagnosis with no unwarranted part or engineer call.
